inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 72.7M common shares on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (2026-07-14) plus ~0.1M dilutive awards (Q2-2026 diluted weighted average 72.9M vs basic 72.8M). Held FLAT because SBC (incl. equity-award tax withholding) is fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution as well would double-count. Buybacks ($2.48B FY2025, $583M H1-2026) are the funded mechanism that keeps the count flat.
inputs.net_debt_note: Q2-2026 10-Q balance sheet (2026-06-30): long-term debt carrying value $6,380.4M (principal $6,425M senior notes, no current portion), cash $356.4M. Operating lease liabilities ($163.8M) are NOT added to debt: lease cost is an operating expense inside EBITDA under ASC 842 (treatment A, charged once).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: MSCI's own FCF definition for FY2025: OCF 1,588.4 - capex 39.3 - capitalized software development costs 90.5 = 1,458.6. The Metrics CSV FreeCashFlow (1,549.1) omits the capitalized-software line (XBRL PaymentsForSoftware), which the component build carries inside capex_pct_path; ties to MSCI's reported Q2-2026 FCF of $326M (370.8 - 11.0 - 33.4).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement share-based compensation add-back $111.8M (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation 111.3; CSV 111.8) PLUS $58.6M of shares withheld for employee taxes on vesting (XBRL AdjustmentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation, netted inside MSCI's 'repurchase of common stock' financing line). MSCI publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure, so the two lines are summed per the house rule. 3-yr combined average is 5.36% of revenue (FY23 4.69%, FY24 5.86%, FY25 5.44%); the withholding component is lumpy because it is marked at vest-date price.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income $16.0M is NOT stripped: MSCI is a net-debt company ($6.0B net debt vs ~$1.3B owner FCF), so there is no cash pile being double-counted. The engine builds unlevered FCF from EBIT, which excludes it anyway.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases $2,484.3M (incl. $58.6M withholding); H1-2026 $583.2M. Debt-funded: senior notes rose from $4.5B to $6.4B over FY2025 to fund an accelerated buyback. Shareholders' equity is -$2.69B as a result; this is capital structure, not distress.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. Risk-free 10y UST ~4.2% (Oct-2026); ERP 5.0%; beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~9.7%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.4% (FY2025 senior-note issuance 5.25-5.75% coupons; FY2025 interest expense $209.9M on ~$5.4B average debt) -> ~4.3% after 20% tax. Market weights at $545: equity $39.7B / debt $6.4B = 86/14 -> WACC 8.9%, rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; risk is carried in the driver paths and the probability weights, not stacked into the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: A: operating leases (liability $163.8M at Q2-2026) stay as operating expense inside EBITDA; no lease liability in net debt, no lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: MSCI has no material non-controlling interest.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1: asset-light, high-margin operating company; subscription + asset-based-fee data/index licensor). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); forecast years are FY2026-FY2035 (10-year horizon because the base-case pre-SBC EBITDA margin is still expanding through year 5 on asset-based-fee operating leverage). COMPONENT ANCHORS FY2025: pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA = operating income 1,713.6 + depreciation 23.4 + intangible amortization 169.5 + SBC 111.8 = 2,018.3 (64.4% of revenue; MSCI's own post-SBC adjusted EBITDA margin 60.8%); D&A 192.9 (6.15%); capex + capitalized software 129.8 (4.14%); cash taxes paid 222.3 = 14.9% of pretax income / GAAP provision 19.5%; deferred-revenue increase 96.4 on a 278.3 revenue increase (35% capture, FY2024 14%). H1-2026 run-rate: revenue +13.1% YoY, pre-SBC EBITDA margin 64.9%, capex+software 4.26% of revenue, cash taxes 25% of pretax (annual true-up timing). Q1-2026 carried a one-off $16.8M tax BENEFIT (net income 406 vs 288.6 a year earlier) that is not in the forward tax path. GUIDANCE CHECK (Q2-2026 call): FY2026 adj-EBITDA expense $1,340-1,370M and FCF $1,485-1,545M; at the modelled 12% revenue growth that implies a post-SBC adjusted EBITDA margin of ~61.5% (model year-1 pre-SBC 64.8% less 3.7% SBC expense = 61.1%); guided FCF midpoint less the $190M SBC+withholding charge gives ~$1.33B of levered owner FCF, versus the model's year-1 unlevered owner FCF of ~$1.62B less ~$0.23B after-tax interest = ~$1.39B, i.e. the model sits ~4% above the guidance midpoint, consistent with MSCI's pattern of raising FCF guidance through the year. Interest expense is running $280M annualized (H1-2026 $140.1M) after the FY2025 debt-funded buyback; it is excluded from unlevered FCF and captured via the $6.0B net-debt deduction. Equity CAGR is not computable (book equity negative since FY2018 from debt-funded buybacks); revenue and owner-FCF CAGRs are the growth anchors.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR unavailable: shareholders' equity has been negative since FY2018 (-$2.69B at Q2-2026) because buybacks exceed retained earnings; a book-value anchor is meaningless for MSCI. Revenue 3-yr CAGR (11.7%) is the anchor for year-1 growth; EPS CAGRs (13-17%) run above revenue because of the shrinking share count (100M -> 73M since 2010).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs use the owner-FCF series (MSCI-definition FCF incl. capitalized software, less SBC and equity-award tax withholding): FY2020 657.9, FY2022 851.7, FY2025 1,288.2. Owner-FCF CAGR (14.8%/14.4%) is ABOVE the reported-FCF CAGR (12.6%/13.9%) because the combined SBC+withholding charge grew more slowly than cash flow (FY2022 withholding was an outsized $112.7M at the 2021 share-price peak); SBC is not eating a rising share of growth here, unlike most US tech names. Periods: FY2020->FY2025 (5-yr) and FY2022->FY2025 (3-yr).

base.narrative: Year-1 growth 12% matches the H1-2026 run-rate (+13.1% reported, +12.2% organic in Q2, total Run Rate +12.0%) with Sustainability & Climate flat; growth then decelerates ~1pp/yr toward 4.5% as asset-based-fee growth normalises from today's +25% run-rate pace. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin expands 64.8% -> 67.5% (post-SBC ~61% -> ~63%) on asset-based-fee operating leverage, held back by the raised FY2026 opex guidance for AI and private-assets investment. Combined SBC+withholding glides 5.4% -> 4.5% of revenue. Capex incl. capitalized software 4.2% -> 3.8%. Cash tax ramps 19% -> 21% (Pillar Two). Working capital captures 12% of the revenue increase (deferred revenue tailwind, 14-35% historically, falling as growth slows).

bull.narrative: Passive shift keeps asset-based fees compounding 20%+ for several years as non-US ETF adoption, custom/direct indexing and thematic products widen the licensing base; Private Capital Solutions (Burgiss) scales into a double-digit-growth third pillar; AI-fuelled analytics lifts pricing. Revenue growth holds 11-13.5% through year 5 and the pre-SBC EBITDA margin reaches 70% (post-SBC ~65%). Terminal growth 3.5% for a business levered to global capital-market growth.

bear.narrative: A 2027-28 equity bear market cuts MSCI-linked ETF AUM ~25% from today's record $2.8T, dropping asset-based-fee revenue (over half of Index) and compressing margins on a fixed cost base; BlackRock-scale clients use the downturn to renegotiate fee rates; Sustainability & Climate shrinks under US political backlash plus EU ESG Rating Regulation compliance costs; S&P DJI and FTSE Russell win share in custom indexes. Growth slows to 2-4% for two years and recovers only to mid-single digits; the pre-SBC margin dips to 62% and recovers to 64%. Terminal growth 2.5%, cap 18x. The balance sheet holds ($6.4B debt vs ~$1.9B EBITDA, no near-term maturities) so this is a valuation, not a solvency, bear case.

scenario_narratives.base: Asset-based fees keep growing with the passive shift but decelerate from +25% run-rate growth; subscription retention holds ~95%; Sustainability & Climate stays flat; Private Assets grows but stays <10% of revenue. Revenue growth 12% fading to 4.5% over ten years, pre-SBC EBITDA margin 64.8% -> 67.5%, combined SBC+withholding 5.4% -> 4.5% of revenue, capex incl. software ~4%, cash tax 19% -> 21%, 9% WACC, 3% terminal growth (Gordon 17.2x binds below the 20x cap).
scenario_narratives.bull: Secular passive flows plus non-US ETF adoption, custom/direct indexing, Private Capital Solutions scaling and AI-driven pricing hold growth at 11-13.5% through year 5 and push the pre-SBC margin to 70%. Terminal growth 3.5% (Gordon 18.8x, under the 20x cap).
scenario_narratives.bear: Equity bear market shrinks ETF AUM and asset-based fees, large clients renegotiate fee rates, ESG stalls under political and regulatory pressure and rivals take custom-index share. Two years of 2-4% growth, margin trough at 62%, recovery to mid-single-digit growth; terminal growth 2.5%, cap 18x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20%: asset-based fees are high-beta to equity-market levels that sit at record highs, the ESG pillar has already stalled (3% growth, flat-to-negative net new sales guided), and client concentration (BlackRock) makes fee renegotiation a live risk. Bull trimmed from 35% to 30%: it needs asset-based-fee growth to stay above 20% from a record run-rate AND Private Assets to scale, two separate things going right. Base 50%: the subscription base (95% retention) makes the central path the most probable.

valuation_philosophy.summary: MSCI is valued as an asset-light compounder on fully SBC-expensed owner FCF, with equity-award tax withholding counted as part of the compensation cost and capitalized software counted as capex (both omitted by the CSV FCF line). The share count is held flat and $6.0B of net debt is deducted; the debt-funded buyback that drove book equity negative is capital structure, not a going-concern issue. The house value is well below the market price: at $545 the market is paying roughly a 7% forward return on the base path, which is the premium a 95%-retention index franchise with secular passive tailwinds has commanded for a decade. The street basis (SBC treated as non-cash) and the required-return table show what return the current price actually implies.
key_risks_to_valuation: Asset-based fees (over half of Index revenue) fall with global equity markets; a 25% drawdown in MSCI-linked ETF AUM is the bear-case trigger
Fee-rate compression from BlackRock and other concentrated ETF sponsors as their AUM scales
Sustainability & Climate segment stall (3% growth) becoming a decline under US political backlash and EU ESG Rating Regulation (July 2026) compliance costs
Debt-funded buybacks at ~$557/share average above the house intrinsic value transfer value from remaining holders if the shares are overpriced; $6.4B gross debt refinances at higher coupons

Combined SBC plus vest-date tax withholding is 5.4% of revenue and lumpy with the share price; the valuation is ~$45/share more sensitive to SBC treatment than the headline suggests (see street basis)
Terminal value is the majority of enterprise value; each 1pp of WACC moves the base value by roughly 15-20%
